proposal.before: Huang led the army in person and captured Xiangping.
proposal.after: Huang campaigned against Liaodong in person and captured Xiangping.
proposal.sourceReason: Restore Liaodong, the target of the personal campaign (自征遼東).

proposal.before: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed at Juqiu, yielded the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the magistrate and capitulated.
proposal.after: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed as magistrate of Jujiu, surrendered the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the county head and capitulated.
proposal.sourceReason: Restore the office 令 and render 居就 as Jujiu in both English fields and repeated uses.

proposal.before: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Juqiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
proposal.after: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Jujiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
proposal.sourceReason: Correct the paired-field Juqiu reading; retain the existing explicit magistrate office.

proposal.before: Because Duan Liao repeatedly was a border trouble, sent general Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong, requesting troops to strike Liao.
proposal.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly caused trouble on the frontier, Huang sent General Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong and request troops to attack Liao.
proposal.sourceReason: The source explicitly makes Huang (皝) the subject, but the existing literal English has no subject before sent. Restore the explicit subject while preserving the general title, repeated frontier trouble, vassalage and troop request.

proposal.before: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
proposal.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you.
proposal.sourceReason: For s0168, explicitly review the documented critical reading: Jinshu jiaozhu says the extant 恨不殺汝 is probably defective for the Tongjian’s 恨恨不欲殺汝; Yulan744 quotes 前燕錄 as 誓不殺汝. Do not treat 恨不 as simply meaning reluctant or silently emend Chinese.

proposal.before: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
proposal.after: I never expected that this resolve would go unfulfilled; I die with lingering regret. It is fate. What can be done!”
proposal.sourceReason: Restore the unexpected failure of his resolve, his lingering regret at death and the final rhetorical question; preserve the closing quotation.

proposal.before: Troubled by Duan Liao, he sent Song Hui to submit to Shi Hu and beg for an allied expedition.
proposal.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly troubled his borders, Huang sent General Song Hui to Shi Hu to declare Huang’s vassalage and request troops to attack Duan Liao.
proposal.sourceReason: Restore repeated border trouble, the general title and the specific request for troops; name Huang explicitly to avoid attributing his vassalage to the envoy.

proposal.before: After a fortnight’s siege his officers begged him to yield.
proposal.after: After the two sides held each other off for more than ten days, his attendants urged Huang to surrender.
proposal.sourceReason: Render 旬餘 as more than ten days, 左右 as attendants, and make Huang the explicit recipient of their advice.

proposal.before: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
proposal.after: Matters came to the point that the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, suddenly passed away.
proposal.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.

proposal.before: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
proposal.after: It came to this: the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
proposal.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.

proposal.before: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
proposal.after: After Duan Liao’s defeat, Murong Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. Believing that his long-established fame and prestige would ultimately endanger his life, he feigned madness, drinking without restraint, letting his hair hang loose, and singing and shouting.
proposal.sourceReason: Restore the omitted 建威 title and the long-established fame and prestige; preserve the complete account of feigned madness.

proposal.before: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
proposal.after: Earlier, when Duan Liao was defeated, Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. He thought that, because his fame and prestige had long been renowned, he would not ultimately be able to remain safe; so he feigned madness, drank without restraint, let his hair hang loose, and sang and shouted.
proposal.sourceReason: Translate 建威 as an office, rather than leaving Jianwei as an apparent personal name; retain all paired-field propositions.

proposal.before: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
proposal.after: Huang secretly sent the merchant Wang Che to observe Han; when Han saw Che he said nothing and only stroked his chest.
proposal.sourceReason: Restore 陰 and the explicit observation target; render 撫膺 without changing it to clutching.

proposal.before: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.
proposal.after: More than a hundred deserving officers were enfeoffed.
proposal.sourceReason: Proposed passive rendering preserves the unexpressed Chinese subject without silently choosing Huang as grantor. This does not resolve the held extraction event attribution.

proposal.before: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
proposal.after: More than a hundred meritorious officials were enfeoffed.
proposal.sourceReason: Preserve the enfeoffment and number without supplying an unexpressed grantor; independently review in the complete imperial-grant context.

proposal.before: Magistrate of Juqiu
proposal.after: Magistrate of Jujiu
proposal.sourceReason: Apply the same source-backed place reading to the title alias; retain alias kind, Chinese witness and person assignment.

proposal.before: surrendered Juqiu
proposal.after: surrendered Jujiu
proposal.sourceReason: Apply the same place reading to the repeated event description; all dateContext and other claim fields remain unchanged.

proposal.before: Jianwei Han
proposal.after: Han, General Who Establishes Might
proposal.sourceReason: Carry the source-backed office translation into the active title alias, retaining the title kind, Chinese witness, evidence and person assignment.

proposal.before: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
proposal.after: Orphaned young, with all his brothers also dying early, he stood utterly alone. None even in his clan recognized his worth; only his uncle Dan thought him extraordinary while he was still young, saying, "This child is not only an outstanding talent of our family but also a fine instrument for serving the age."
proposal.sourceReason: 雖宗族無能識者 means none of the clan recognized his worth, not merely that few knew him; 幼 refers to Yu when Dan recognized his promise.

proposal.before: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
proposal.after: You follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Confucius; surely your insight into the first signs of change is also extraordinary.”
proposal.sourceReason: 知機其神 concerns discerning incipient opportunities or changes; Heaven calling is not in this Chinese unit. This repeated Yi/Confucius use is reviewed independently of s0193.

proposal.before: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.
proposal.after: When the capital was moved to Helong, Yang Yu, who had long possessed an ingenious mind, drew up the plans for all the city walls, moats, palaces and gates that Murong Huang built.
proposal.sourceReason: 城池宮闔 includes moats and the palace/gate complex; wall and tower alone omits these objects and does not express 皆裕之規模 as Yu’s plans.

proposal.before: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
proposal.after: Although Yang Yu had served Murong Huang for only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble, respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading posts at court, he lived like a scholar in plain clothes.
proposal.sourceReason: 仕皝日近 means his service under Huang was recent or short, not that he grew daily closer to Huang. The complete unit retains the contrast in rank and his personal qualities.

proposal.before: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.
proposal.after: For displaced and isolated gentlemen who died, he invariably arranged their collection and burial, cared for the orphans and bereaved they left, and devoted himself to receiving gentlemen, worthy or unworthy alike; thus he was esteemed wherever he went.
proposal.sourceReason: 經營收葬 and 存恤孤遺 distinguish burial arrangements from care for survivors; 士無賢不肖皆傾身待之 explicitly includes worthy and unworthy, a distinction omitted by the current English.
